facebook.content_angle: Six-beat kick efficiency — how most club swimmers kick from the knee and lose propulsion, versus the hip-driven six-beat kick pattern elite swimmers use to add 10% to their 50m speed
facebook.post_text:
Most swimmers kick wrong — and they're bleeding speed every single lap. 🦵

If your kick feels like hard work but isn't moving you faster, the problem isn't fitness. It's mechanics. Knee-driven kicking kills propulsion and tanks your body position at the same time.

Here's what elite swimmers do differently:
👉 The kick initiates from the hip, not the knee — a tight, rhythmic six-beat pattern that stabilises rotation and adds propulsion simultaneously
👉 Each kick is compact and continuous — no wide, slow cycles that create drag and disrupt your stroke tempo
👉 Swimmers who switch to a proper six-beat pattern have recorded up to 10.21% improvement in 50m times — without changing anything else

That's not a marginal gain. That's a race-changing difference. 🔥

✔️ Kick from the hip, not the knee
✔️ Keep ankle relaxed — not rigid, not floppy
✔️ Practice with a kickboard at low speed before integrating at pace

This autumn training block is the perfect time to rebuild the fundamentals that will make or break your racing in spring.
